## 固定收益市場主線

10月2日美國就業報告明顯轉弱，市場對聯準會立即升息的預期下降，美國公債卻未能守住早盤漲勢。週五尾盤10年期指標債殖利率約為5.27%，Bloomberg的10年期每日殖利率則上升5.7個基點至5.273%。9月就業人口僅增加2.9萬人，薪資年增率降至2021年以來最低。這讓決策官員有更多空間等待，卻沒有帶來長期借款成本的持續下降。

當天行情顯示，對下一次政策會議的疑慮緩解，不等於整體融資壓力解除。美國投資級與高收益債利差小幅收窄，硬通貨計價的新興市場債利差明顯收窄，扭轉前一天普遍惡化的走勢。債市吐回漲幅時，股市仍保住漲幅。G7同意釋出緊急石油與柴油庫存，也緩和燃料價格疑慮，但固定收益市場收盤時，布蘭特原油仍高於每桶$102。

歐洲方面，槓桿部位進一步解除，凸顯市場承接賣壓的困難，法國10年期公債相對德國的利差擴大至154個基點，為2011年以來最高。通膨逼近4%，主權融資條件卻已產生部分緊縮效果，讓歐洲央行面臨更尖銳的取捨。企業融資也發出另一種警訊：AI基礎設施的新融資計畫陸續出現，與此同時，新債認購反應轉弱，再融資成本上升。週五就業數據不如預期，改變的是政策行動的急迫性，並未減少政府與企業仍須籌措的資金。

## 就業放緩，美國公債漲勢卻未能延續

9月非農就業增加2.9萬人，不僅低於市場預期的9萬人，也低於彭博經濟學家調查中的所有預測。8月增幅下修至13.3萬人，前兩個月合計亦遭下修。失業率由4.1%升至4.2%，經濟學家原本預期持平。招聘與薪資同時走弱，使這份報告呈現的情況不只是一般性的就業增速降溫。

民間雇主增加4.6萬個職位，低於預期的8.5萬人及8月修正後的8.9萬人；政府就業減少1.7萬人，前月修正後則增加4.4萬人。製造業增加9,000人，對照預期1萬人及前月修正後的1.5萬人。地方政府、資訊業、專業與商業服務，以及金融活動均減少職位，醫療與休閒餐旅業則持續招聘。資料中心及其他AI基礎設施投資，仍支撐營建與製造業就業。

除整體增幅偏低，招聘分布也值得注意。衡量就業成長廣度的擴散指數降至10月以來最低，失業期間中位數升至11.5週、為四個月高點。黑人失業率達7%，部分原因是勞動參與率提高。招聘放緩並非均勻分布在各產業；裁員仍少，也不代表求職容易。

不過，家庭調查呈現的情況，比單看企業調查的就業人數穩健。家庭調查的另一項就業指標大增，勞動參與率由61.6%升至61.8%，為四個月高點；範圍較廣的U-6失業率由7.7%降至7.6%，為2025年1月以來最低。Glenmede的Jason Pride認為，整體失業率上升，部分反映民眾有信心重返勞動市場，不能全歸因於原有勞工陷入困境。Regions Financial首席經濟學家Richard Moody則形容，經濟仍處於招聘少、裁員也少的狀態。

對貨幣政策而言，薪資帶來的變化更直接。平均時薪月增0.1%，低於預期的0.3%及8月的0.3%；年增率由3.1%降至3%，低於預期的3.2%，也是2021年以來最弱增幅。每週平均工時維持34.4小時，預期為34.3小時。即使就業與工時沒有實際下降，薪資增速放緩已削弱勞動需求推高通膨的論據。

Oxford Economics的Michael Pearce判斷，勞動市場依然穩健，但並未製造通膨。Jefferies的Thomas Simons表示，報告強力支持10月暫停升息，因此改變原先預期連續升息25個基點的看法。包括Oscar Munoz在內的TD Securities策略師，將升息預測由10月與1月改為12月與3月。American Century的Charles Tan則保留條件：這份報告為按兵不動提供更多依據，但再有一至兩筆通膨數據，仍可能讓判斷轉趨鷹派。

公債最初反應強烈。2年期殖利率一度下降多達10個基點，隨後反彈，至紐約接近中午時已較前一日高出逾1個基點、接近4.81%。彭博在數據公布後的報導中，10年期殖利率最初下降約3個基點至5.21%。利率交換將10月升息機率由公布前接近30%降至約20%，一度也不再完全反映12月以前再升息一次。但到交易日結束，交易員又預期年底前會有一次升息；利率市場報導中的明年底前升息三次預期仍未改變。

行情反轉後，Bloomberg每日殖利率序列的主要年期全面上升。2年期上升4.2個基點至4.827%，5年期上升4.8個基點至5.054%，30年期上升1.4個基點至5.621%；2年與10年期利差擴大1.5個基點至44.6個基點，2年與30年期利差則收窄2.8個基點至79.4個基點。10年期實質殖利率上升2.7個基點至2.909%，同系列損益兩平通膨率上升3個基點至2.364%。因此，名目殖利率當天上升5.7個基點，是實質借款成本提高與長期通膨補償增加共同反映的結果。

拉長比較期間，這股壓力更明顯。10年期殖利率較一個月前高47.4個基點，實質殖利率高46.8個基點，損益兩平通膨率僅增加0.6個基點。Pimco總裁Christian Stracke將實質利率整體上升，主要歸因於超大型雲端業者與AI生態系的資金需求，並以Micron上調資本支出估計為例。他也認為，AI借款人在投資級債中的占比提高，可能推升整體利差，而不代表每家成分發行人的信用品質都同步惡化。就這段較長期間而言，這與通膨預期推高殖利率的解釋不同，也使融資供給在就業數據偏弱後仍居於核心。

達拉斯聯準銀行總裁Lorie Logan週四的談話，於本次報導期間內公開，為政策判斷補上不同條件。她今年具有FOMC投票權，估計為平衡就業與通膨風險，目標利率區間仍須再提高至少50個基點。她區分了兩種殖利率上升來源：成長較強、中性利率較高，以及期限溢價增加。後者可能抑制活動，減少聯準會自身緊縮的必要性；她仍主張維持適度限制性的政策立場。

這比副主席Philip Jefferson、紐約聯準銀行總裁John Williams及負責監理的副主席Michelle Bowman已表達的耐心立場更強硬。週五就業報告為耐心等待提供新的經濟依據，而非另一個新的領導層訊號。前Bridgewater策略師Rebecca Patterson提醒，9月一致通過升息後，10月可能出現異議。她認為，維持就業穩定所需的增幅接近零，即使僅增加2.9萬人仍屬正成長，因此下一次決策究竟應以通膨或招聘降溫為重，仍有爭論空間。

工廠訂單提供另一筆較不受矚目、但好壞參半的需求資訊。8月訂單月增0.1%，符合預期；7月增幅由0.9%下修至0.8%。扣除運輸的訂單增加0.3%，扣除國防增加0.1%。機械訂單增加1.1%，前月為1.5%；電氣設備、家電及零組件由零成長轉為增加1%；基本金屬增加1.2%，前月為2.1%。非國防飛機與零件訂單減少4.3%，金屬製品減少1.4%。細項顯示部分投資類別需求仍在、其他領域偏弱，並不是繼就業數據之後的第二個全面收縮訊號。

風險資產保住較多最初的利多反應。標普500收漲0.73%至7,722.72，那斯達克100上漲1%至30,807.93，半導體股上漲2.40%；VIX降至15.31。美元指數下跌0.17%至101.93，彭博另一項美元指標下跌0.3%，創一個月來最差單日表現，但全週仍上漲約0.8%。黃金也未能延續初步反應：現貨金最初一度上漲1.2%，至紐約時間下午1時35分卻下跌0.92%至每盎司$4,139.13。債市反轉，持續影響那些價格會隨付息證券報酬變動的資產。

## 法國利差擴大，加深歐洲央行抗通膨難題

法國10年期公債相對德國的利差，週五達154個基點，超過週四尾盤報導的141個基點，進一步升至2011年以來最寬。預算案公布未能止住賣壓，新報導也更清楚揭示，集中持有的槓桿部位如何將財政疑慮轉為劇烈行情。

據熟悉交易人士透露，Taula Capital Management、Balyasny Asset Management等機構，先前利用法國公債殖利率與利率交換的差距建立利差收益部位，週四債券下跌時急於解除。RBC BlueBay的Kaspar Hense表示，押注曲線變陡及做多法國公債的部位，都觸發停損。Fidelity的Marion Le Morhedec估計，避險基金可能占目前利差交易活動的一半；投資人結構愈來愈依賴快速進出的資金，使市場承受更多壓力。

長期投資人也在調整配置，但撤離程度並不一致。三井住友DS資產管理的Shinji Kunibe表示，其全球固定收益基金已賣出全部法國公債，多數資金轉入德國公債，部分轉入短期日本公債。他以法國財政的不確定性，對照日本對投資計畫成本愈來愈充分的溝通。Credit Agricole Assurances的Florence Barjou仍將法國視為核心持倉，但表示保險公司正分散配置；今年上半年其法國主權債持有額約€610億。這並非機構投資人一致放棄法國。

義大利10年期對德國利差週五為127個基點，全週有望錄得2020年3月以來最大擴幅，西班牙利差亦擴大。週末回顧本週交易的報導，將比利時與希臘列入受影響市場，同時指出跌勢大致於週五穩定、較長年期債券回升。Morgan Stanley Investment Management的Jeff Mueller認為，已出現初步蔓延跡象；若價格持續不規則波動，決策官員可能須更密切注意。區內多數市場的利差仍遠低於過去危機的極端水準，但重定價速度，使跨市場傳導成為眼前關切。

瑞士法郎顯示，投資人不只在歐元區債市內避險，也在區外尋求保護。法郎兩天內對歐元升值約1.8%，週五歐元兌法郎降至約0.93、為兩個月低點；週四CME成交量約為今年平均的四倍。Commerzbank的Michael Pfister以瑞士較均衡的預算為由，預期一年後匯價為0.91。這波走勢重新帶動法郎需求，此前其低利息報酬曾使吸引力下降。

同一天，歐洲央行的通膨問題更加突出。9月歐元區消費者物價年增3.8%，高於預期的3.7%及8月的3.2%，達三年高點；核心通膨如預期升至2.5%，服務通膨為3.2%。區域數據確認先前各國已公布的超預期升幅，能源仍是加速的主要來源。歐盟執委會調查亦顯示，各產業售價預期高於長期平均，家庭對未來一年通膨的預期明顯上升。

但彭博經濟研究的David Powell認為，升息急迫性沒有整體數字看來那麼高。整體與核心通膨的季度平均值，大致仍符合歐洲央行預測；機票基期效應推高基礎通膨，但服務通膨動能減弱。再加上主權殖利率急升，他預期10月不升息，12月可能作最後一次升息。美國就業數據公布後，貨幣市場更傾向歐洲央行再升息兩次、而非三次，英國央行再升息三次、而非四次；就在週二，市場對兩者都曾反映逾100個基點的升幅。

難題不只在下一次利率決策。歐洲央行尚未動用的傳導保護工具（TPI），旨在應對不合理、無序且損害貨幣政策傳導的市場動態。Danske Bank的Piet Christiansen認為，法國的財政立場與政治不確定性足以支持較寬利差，因而讓干預理由更難成立。買債紓緩壓力，可能被視為融通赤字，也會在央行仍努力遏制通膨時放鬆金融條件。

Citigroup的Jamie Searle提出，暫停量化緊縮可能是較早採取的措施。恢復到期資金再投資，可減少對價格敏感的買家須承接的債務。Allianz Trade的Ana Boata估計，歐洲央行持有的法國債券每月約有€50億到期，相當於新發行額約20%。因此，即使不直接承諾壓低某一法國利差水準，調整資產負債表政策仍可能產生實際影響。

目前兩種干預都未宣布。德國央行總裁Joachim Nagel強調2%的通膨目標，而非特定利差水準；法國央行總裁Emmanuel Moulin則警告，歐洲央行沒有神奇解方。Global Sovereign Advisory的Anne-Laure Kiechel認為，法德利差接近175至180個基點時可能促成行動，但這是她的判斷，並非歐洲央行門檻。Candriam投資長Nicolas Forest指出，直接貨幣交易（OMT）另有障礙：必須正式提出援助請求，而若由Le Pen或Mélenchon執政，這會是政治上困難的一步。

其他地區的財政選擇，也未順應放寬預算限制的呼聲。義大利最後階段削減原定國防支出，以將赤字降到歐盟3%的上限以下。歐盟官員警告，尋求能源補助豁免的政府，低估了市場對可預測性的需求。芬蘭的Olli Rehn表示，較高借款成本與有限財政空間，可能暴露金融體系其他地方的弱點，持續財政整頓仍是政府的責任。新的市場壓力，並未促成放寬財政限制的共識。

## AI融資擴張，新債需求卻轉趨不穩

Broadcom的承銷團開始籌集$600億新的AI晶片融資，預計使Anthropic及其他企業受益。據熟悉計畫人士透露，Blackstone牽頭方案中的銀行，正為$420億A類優先擔保融資準備聯貸文件。投資人已在消化龐大的收購與基礎設施借款，此案規模使其認購反應的影響遠超單一交易。

Amazon則探索另一條路徑。《金融時報》報導，公司正商討將約$80億高階Nvidia晶片移出資產負債表，轉入由外部投資人融資的特殊目的公司。擬納入的資產包括分布在十多座美國資料中心的數千顆Grace Blackwell晶片。另一邊，由Nvidia支持的澳洲營運商Firmus Grid，將擬議IPO定價為每股A$11，目標至少募集A$50億，隱含估值約A$300億。債務聯貸、外部資產融資與公開股權，提供了支應同一資本密集型擴張的不同方式。

SoftBank的表現顯示，股東熱情與債權人戒心可能分歧。股價四週上漲24%，9月錄得四個月來首次單月上漲，信用違約交換（CDS）卻升至2023年以來最高。SoftBank持有晶片設計商Arm近90%股權，Arm股價9月回升約20%，有助其資產價值；但9月29日SoftBank相對淨資產價值的折價仍達24%，高於今年迄今平均20%。Sparx Asset Management的Han Jiho認為，CDS若持續擴大，可能限制底層資產進一步上漲對股價的助益。

股價回升並未消除昂貴的債務融資。SoftBank最近$111億的非投資級債發行中，一筆7.5年期債券殖利率達9.75%。Bernstein的David Dai看好Arm在代理式AI與伺服器CPU的潛力，估計CPU市場規模可能達$3,300億。Resona的Hiroki Takei認為，目前獲利提供融資能力，較高借款成本屬尾端風險，但也提醒，槓桿可能放大未來AI反轉的衝擊。兩人的樂觀看法，仰賴資產成長與創造現金的能力，而非債權人降低要求的報酬。

整體初級市場展望更為審慎。週末報導指出，Campbell's及Bain Capital Credit的私募信貸基金發債需求平淡，烏茲別克的Multinational Mine Group則擱置5年期債券發行。本週僅四家借款人進入美國高評級債市場。10月投資級債預期發行約$1,000億，低於2025年10月的$1,320億及9月近$1,950億；但今年迄今發行額仍增加約30%。

Paramount新債掛牌後走弱，已揭示這項困難；週五新增披露則量化了發行人得到的定價利益及仍須負擔的利息。財務長Dennis Cinelli表示，行銷期間借款成本降低37.5個基點，每年節省約$2億。定價收緊時部分投資人退出，使留下來的投資人獲配量超出預期。交易能完成，卻不代表債券之後容易分銷。Cinelli及Citi的Leon Kalvaria仍肯定融資的長期目的與完成情況，買方則先承受價格折損。

另一篇週末報導，指出Paramount與Oracle之間更具體的信用連結。投資人透過Larry Ellison，愈來愈將兩家公司的違約風險視為相關，債務保險成本逐漸接近並同步波動。家族信託為約$470億收購股權融資中的相當一部分提供保證，家族也承諾採取措施協助Paramount降槓桿。然而，Ellison大部分財富仍繫於Oracle股票，而Oracle自身正以舉債推動AI建設。

依彭博富豪估計，Ellison財富已較高峰減少近$2,000億，但仍約有$1,920億。Oracle長期債務兩年內近乎翻倍，超過$1,600億，成為美國公司債市場第五大借款人。標普7月將Oracle降至BBB-，9月將Paramount發行人評等降至BB。Wellington的Campe Goodman認為，共同支持者形成合併風險曝險；標普的Jawad Hussain則指出，Oracle股價下跌，可能恰在Paramount需要資金時削弱家族支援能力。這項連結關乎承諾背後的財力，而非兩家公司業務相同。

全球公司債利差全週擴大約5個基點，至半年來最寬。全球市場殖利率與既有票息的差距達1.23個百分點，高於2月的0.17個百分點，反映汰換舊債的成本增加。這些全週情況，與週五美國整體信用利差小幅收窄並存。隨美國公債殖利率再度上升，總報酬仍受影響：LQD經配息調整的單日報酬為負0.20%，HYG約上漲0.01%，EMB下跌0.13%。

Barclays策略師Harry Mateer與Dominique Toublan週五指出，10年期美國公債殖利率在一個月內上升至少40個基點，通常是公司債利差隨後擴大的前兆。PGIM的David Del Vecchio認為，利率波動比利差本身更直接限制需求；較高的整體殖利率終究可能吸引退休基金及其他收益型買家，但投資人希望利率更穩定，再積極投入資金。週五利差收窄，並未解決基礎融資利率究竟會落在何處的不確定性。

## 地產、私募信貸與主權債務揭露受檢視

以地產為主的銀行，是歐洲次順位債明顯的弱點。Deutsche Pfandbriefbank（PBB）的AT1債券跌破每€1面額的€0.80，為歐洲9月表現最差的AT1債。該行一筆€3億債券的首次可贖回日期已過三年，8月以來跌逾9%。Landesbank Baden-Württemberg（LBBW）一筆€7.5億、2030年可贖回的債券，週五指示價格一年多來首次低於面額。

經歐元避險的AT1指數，8月以來由獲利轉為總報酬損失2%。PBB稱商用不動產融資是業務核心，LBBW近五分之一曝險則與地產相關。高利率削弱物業價值與借款人財務指標，既增加既有貸款壓力，也減少新放貸機會。TwentyFour的Jakub Lichwa表示，部分德國銀行的商用不動產組合，在最新利率引發的拋售前已轉弱，現在承受重疊壓力。銀行業以外，德國公寓買家Net Zero Properties即使改善條件，仍未取得足夠需求，放棄€5億借款計畫。

據熟悉討論人士透露，Bain Capital正探索投資香港新世界發展，可能與控股鄭氏家族的新資金一同進場。新世界6月底債務約HK$1,430億，部分於2028年到期。洽談消息一度推升股價，但週五香港時間下午3時43分又下跌2.3%。磋商尚在進行，交易並不確定；目前是負債沉重的開發商可能取得新支持，尚非已達成的資本重整。

私募信貸投資人持續面臨流動性限制。Blue Owl再次將兩檔基金季度贖回限制在5%。規模約$50億、聚焦科技的OTIC，第三季股東申請贖回39%股份，略高於前季的38.1%；最新一次付款完成後，六個月累計提供的流動性將約為$4.46億，相當於原始贖回申請的35%。規模$350億的Blue Owl Credit Income Corp.，申請比例由18.8%降至16.8%，但仍遠高於實際贖回量。

在贖回要求持續之際，估值方式也受到官方更密切注意。SEC工作人員聲明要求業者改善私募持倉估值，以及風險與價值揭露，但沒有新增規則。Apollo週四開始在其$8,500億信用業務推行每日報價；Ares另外為首檔次級市場基金募集$42億，超過初始目標四倍，向私募管理機構提供資金。這些措施透過不同管道處理估值頻率與流動性供給，均未改變Blue Owl的贖回條款。

加彭的主權債務揭露問題，直接影響籌資。擬議$5.8億債券的投資人電話會議上，市場質疑其合併債務CFA9.53兆、約$163億，以及2027年赤字預測為GDP的5.4%。債務數字比9月13日公布的CFA11.7兆估計低19%，卻高於7月公布的2025年底CFA9.4兆。7月配套聲明曾讓部分投資人預期，審計後債務會大幅下降，之後的說明因而難以與這項期待相符。

加彭2033年美元債殖利率全週一度上升多達150個基點，至紀錄高點13.1%，週五才回落到約12.98%。截至10月2日當週，加彭美元債為邊境主權債中表現最弱。電話會議參與者表示，殖利率上升可能妨礙擬議發行，政府則未說是否延後。問題不只是全球殖利率上升，而是投資人質疑已揭露負債究竟如何變動。

印尼新任財政部長則嘗試釐清機構權責。Suahasil Nazara週五表示，將把赤字控制在法律規定GDP的3%上限內，貨幣政策與Danantara主權財富基金則各自依職掌運作。2026與2027年預算都未納入Danantara股利，有別於前任試圖為國庫取得近$70億的做法。他也排除恢復每日政府公債買回，認為目前情況不足以啟動穩定機制，並形容印尼與美國10年期利差約220至225個基點屬健康水準。

Suahasil表示，繼5月$34.5億美元與歐元債交易後，本季仍可能再發全球債。2036年4月美元債對美國公債利差約106個基點，為約兩個月最寬。預算預測仍具挑戰：今年赤字預期為2.85%，2027年降至2.4%，假設油價每桶$75、平均匯率每美元兌17,500印尼盾；實際油價已逾$100，印尼盾接近18,000。他捍衛與Danantara的協調，但未直接化解Fitch與Moody's將展望改為負面時提出、整體赤字以外的財政風險疑慮。

市政信用也有自身的籌資抉擇。曼哈頓Nightingale-Bamford School計畫在募款持續進行時，動用約$1,000萬不受限制的準備金支應體育設施工程；Moody's因而將其評等由A3降至Baa1，展望由負面改為穩定。2025會計年度未償債務近$6,400萬，工程成本定為$9,000萬。Moody's指出，資本募款計畫及募款主管異動帶來推進與治理風險，但仍肯定招生需求、定價能力、營運改善與流動性。工程仍按進度推進，且未超出預算。

## 通膨分歧與制度新進展

東京9月核心消費者物價年增率由1.8%加速至2.7%，高於預測中位數2.3%，也是1月以來首次重返2%以上。排除生鮮食品與能源的通膨由2%升至3%。托育與水費減免到期貢獻相當大，但政府能源補貼仍使整體指標降低近0.4個百分點。

細項不只反映臨時優惠取消。加工食品價格上漲3.6%；帝國資料銀行指出，主要食品與飲料企業9月調漲4,965項商品價格，為一年前的兩倍以上。自來水服務費用上升約66%，住宿價格由年減1.4%轉為年增4.6%，服務價格上漲2.3%，為2023年11月以來最強增幅。第一生命的Yoshiki Shinke預期日本央行12月升息，認為即使扣除臨時措施影響，成本上升仍正傳導給消費者。

經濟政策大臣木內實，則對先前日本不再需要貨幣寬鬆的說法補充限定。他週五表示，所指是殖利率曲線控制等非常規工具，該措施已於2024年3月結束；至於一般貨幣寬鬆是否仍有必要，他拒絕表態，也不願詳述內閣府代表在9月會議上對中性利率的談話。這項澄清顯示，政府是否接受進一步常規升息，沒有部分投資人先前從部長發言推斷得那麼明確。

澳洲債券的相對表現朝不同方向發展。10年期殖利率僅比美國同年期高約12個基點，接近2025年9月以來最窄差距。Barrenjoey與Westpac預期未來數月將收斂；NAB的Kenneth Crompton表示，倒掛可能早於其2027年基本情境，若政策預期分歧足夠大，明年底差距可能再回到負20個基點。澳洲公債9月下跌1%，美國公債跌2.2%。除了已報導的澳洲央行政策決定，澳洲的財政狀況與較小的AI融資需求，也是相對差異來源；但對美國利率的敏感度，以及國內通膨再起，仍限制相對表現進一步改善。

新的研究量化了英國額外的融資成本。彭博經濟研究估計，指標債的信譽溢價約30個基點，到2029至2030年會帶來每年£25億的額外利息成本。Schroders的James Bilson認為，部分困難在於聲譽；RBC的Cathal Kennedy則指出，市場對多次未能兌現的財政計畫抱持懷疑。這個估計是全球殖利率上升中的英國特有成本，並非長期英國公債再度突破6%的新里程碑。

英國地方借款也可能改變。政府鼓勵英格蘭市長考慮，以擬議的過夜旅客稅收入為基礎借款；法案尚待提出，地方計畫預期於2028年初之前完成。UKHospitality的Allen Simpson反對，指出反對黨已承諾取消此稅，可能移除長期債務所仰賴的收入。方案可提前進行基礎設施支出，但承諾收入在政治上能否持久，仍有爭議。

美國方面，Scope週五聲明維持AA-主權評等及穩定展望，同時警告，巨額赤字使美國愈來愈容易受到投資人情緒變化影響。除非成長明顯轉強或進行財政調整，它預期十年內債務將達產出的160%，到2031年淨利息成本將異常高昂。評等未變，伴隨的是對中期債務軌跡更明確的警告，而非再次降評。

聯準會治理也出現新決定。司法部長Todd Blanche週五表示，不會僅依監察長對整修工程的調查結果，重啟對前主席Jerome Powell的刑事調查；若獨立審計發現犯罪行為，仍可能促成調查。週日，國家經濟委員會主任Kevin Hassett要求Powell離開理事會，並表示不贊同9月升息，但尊重主席Kevin Warsh的理由。這是在Blanche決定之後、週末重新出現的政治壓力，與週五債市交易屬不同時點的發展。

歐洲央行接班討論也向前推進。據熟悉商議人士透露，德國總理Friedrich Merz計畫在未來幾天會晤Klaas Knot，並於未來幾週會晤Pablo Hernández de Cos。這些接觸顯示，柏林不再考慮由Joachim Nagel接任總裁。義大利的Giancarlo Giorgetti週五要求Lagarde更清楚說明自己的未來。既有接班程序因而增加了具體會面及公開要求說明，但總裁人選仍未決定。

財政部長Scott Bessent在週六刊出的Axios訪問中，回應殖利率上升引發的債市拋售。他認為，這是全球而非美國獨有的升勢，不必驚慌，並強調消費與薪資成長強勁，預期與伊朗相關的能源衝擊終會消退。他的信心，與持續高融資成本如何影響經濟較弱環節的疑慮形成對照。Franklin Templeton的Max Gokhman估計，美國非金融企業債只有約13%、約$5,700億在2027年到期，許多既有屋主也保有平均約4%的房貸利率。這些緩衝會延後高新借款利率的影響，使高利率持續多久更重要，而不是消除曝險。

## 後續市場觀察重點

下一個美國成長檢驗是10月5日紐約時間上午9時45分公布的標普全球服務業與綜合PMI終值。服務業預期58.7、前值56.5，綜合預期58.4、前值56；上午10時接著公布ISM服務業指數，預期55.7、前值55.4。在招聘偏弱的背景下，服務需求強勁與經濟全面放緩會帶來不同解讀，價格與招聘細項也將影響再升息的剩餘理由。10月6日ADP每週就業資料，以及10月8日失業救濟申請，將補上更即時的勞動觀察；首次申請預期19.5萬人、前值19.7萬人。

聯準會9月會議紀錄週三公布，歐洲央行會議紀要則在週四。兩者記載的都是週五就業報告及最新法國利差壓力出現前的決策，重點在於條件改變後，當時的通膨疑慮是否仍具持續性。Williams、Bowman與Logan預定10月6日發言，將就耐心等待、進一步緊縮，以及市場殖利率上升的作用，提供不同觀點。10月14日美國CPI，仍是10月27至28日聯準會會議前的重要通膨檢驗。

未來一週的3年、10年及30年期美國公債標售，將在就業報告未能帶來持續漲勢後測試需求。3年期標售定於10月6日，較長年期則最直接面對資金競爭。公司債交易商預期當週美國高評級債發行$250億至$300億；受訪歐洲專業人士逾80%預期發行超過€250億。新債反應將顯示，有吸引力的絕對殖利率是否開始抵銷利率不穩定的影響。Broadcom擬議聯貸另將測試投資人對AI融資的意願；Paramount收購預計10月6日交割，債務配售後，注意力將轉向交易落實。

歐元區財長週四在盧森堡開會，能源支持、財政彈性及法國債市動盪都迫使議程作出回應。若壓力進一步蔓延到其他主權債，貨幣傳導及歐洲央行資產負債表應對的問題將更尖銳。日本週二公布8月薪資，將檢驗實質薪資成長是否延續到第八個月；印度週三政策決策，預期將附買回利率升至5.5%。英國10月28日預算案，必須同時處理財政計畫所承受的信譽溢價與全球利率上升。

能源方面，緊急庫存釋出已由討論變成宣布。G7與夥伴週五同意，在四個月內供應最多1億桶石油與柴油，由國際能源署（IEA）協調，初期以柴油為重點。協議降低美國禁止柴油出口的可能性，消息也壓低歐洲柴油與布蘭特價格。週五固定收益市場收盤時，WTI下跌1.90%至$91.11，布蘭特僅下跌0.06%至$102.25，全週仍上漲4.94%。煉製燃料送達消費者的速度，仍會實質影響通膨與財政補助需求。

long_thesis.english_markdown:
## Opening Fixed-Income Thesis

Treasuries surrendered an early rally on October 2 even after a sharply weaker U.S. employment report reduced expectations of an immediate Federal Reserve rate increase. The benchmark 10-year yield was around 5.27% late Friday, while Bloomberg's dated 10-year yield rose 5.7 basis points to 5.273%. Employers added only 29,000 jobs in September and wage growth slowed to its weakest annual pace since 2021. That combination gave policymakers more room to wait, but it did not secure a lasting reduction in the cost of long-term borrowing.

The session separated relief over the next policy meeting from the pressures on financing more broadly. U.S. investment-grade and high-yield spreads tightened modestly, and hard-currency emerging-market spreads tightened noticeably, reversing the previous day's broad deterioration. Equities retained their gains as bonds lost theirs. A G7 agreement to release emergency oil and diesel stocks eased fuel-price anxiety, although Brent remained above $102 a barrel at the fixed-income close.

In Europe, France's 10-year premium over Germany reached 154 basis points, its widest since 2011, as further exits from leveraged positions exposed the difficulty of absorbing selling. The ECB faced a sharper conflict between inflation approaching 4% and sovereign financing conditions that were already doing part of the tightening. Corporate funding supplied a separate warning: fresh financing plans for AI infrastructure arrived alongside weaker new-issue reception and rising refinancing costs. Friday's jobs disappointment changed the urgency of policy, not the volume of capital that governments and companies still needed to raise.

## Hiring Slows, but the Treasury Rally Fades

September nonfarm payrolls rose 29,000 against a 90,000 consensus, missing every estimate in Bloomberg's economist survey. August's gain was revised down to 133,000, and the preceding two months were revised lower overall. Unemployment increased to 4.2% from 4.1%, where economists had expected it to remain. The release replaced the prospect of a routine hiring slowdown with evidence of substantially weaker recruitment and softer wages at the same time.

Private employers added 46,000 jobs, below the 85,000 consensus and a revised 89,000 in August. Government employment fell 17,000 after a revised 44,000 increase. Manufacturing added 9,000, compared with expectations of 10,000 and a revised 15,000 previously. Local government lost jobs, as did information, professional and business services, and financial activities. Healthcare and leisure and hospitality continued hiring, while data-center and other AI infrastructure investment supported construction and manufacturing employment.

That unevenness matters alongside the small headline gain. The diffusion index measuring the breadth of payroll growth fell to its lowest since October. Median unemployment duration increased to a four-month high of 11.5 weeks, and Black unemployment reached 7%, partly because participation increased. Recruitment was not slowing equally across sectors, and the persistence of low dismissals did not make finding a new job straightforward.

The household survey nevertheless offered a less fragile picture than the establishment count alone. Its separate employment measure surged, while participation rose to a four-month high of 61.8% from 61.6%. The broader U-6 unemployment rate declined to 7.6% from 7.7%, its lowest since January 2025. Glenmede's Jason Pride interpreted the increase in the headline jobless rate as partly reflecting confidence among people returning to the workforce, rather than simply distress among existing workers. Regions Financial chief economist Richard Moody described a continuing low-hire, low-fire economy.

Wages supplied the more direct change for monetary policy. Average hourly earnings increased 0.1% monthly, below the 0.3% consensus and August's 0.3% rise. Annual growth slowed to 3% from 3.1%, against expectations of 3.2%, reaching its weakest pace since 2021. Average weekly hours remained at 34.4, compared with a forecast of 34.3. Slower pay gains reduced the argument that labor demand was adding to inflation, without requiring an outright fall in employment or hours.

Oxford Economics' Michael Pearce judged that the labor market remained solid but was not generating inflation. Jefferies' Thomas Simons said the report strongly favored an October pause, changing his earlier expectation of successive quarter-point increases. TD Securities strategists including Oscar Munoz shifted their forecast to increases in December and March instead of October and January. American Century's Charles Tan was more conditional: the report provided additional cover to hold, but another one or two inflation observations could restore a more hawkish assessment.

The initial bond response was forceful. Two-year yields briefly fell as much as 10 basis points before rebounding to more than 1 basis point higher on the day, near 4.81%, by late morning in New York. In Bloomberg's post-release account, the 10-year was initially down about 3 basis points at 5.21%. Interest-rate swaps reduced the chance of an October increase to about 20% from nearly 30% before the release and briefly stopped fully pricing another increase by December. By the end of the session, traders again anticipated a year-end move; expectations for three increases by the end of next year remained intact in the rates account.

The reversal left Bloomberg's dated yields higher across the principal maturities. The two-year rose 4.2 basis points to 4.827%, the five-year increased 4.8 to 5.054%, and the 30-year rose 1.4 to 5.621%. The 2s10s spread widened 1.5 basis points to 44.6, while 2s30s narrowed 2.8 to 79.4. At 10 years, the real yield increased 2.7 basis points to 2.909%, while same-series breakeven inflation rose 3 to 2.364%. Both higher real borrowing costs and increased long-term inflation compensation contributed to the nominal yield's 5.7-basis-point daily rise.

The persistence is substantial over a longer comparison. The 10-year yield was 47.4 basis points above its level a month earlier, and its real counterpart was up 46.8, while the breakeven increased only 0.6. Pimco President Christian Stracke attributed the broader rise in real rates primarily to demand for capital from hyperscalers and the AI ecosystem, citing Micron's higher capital-expenditure estimates. He also argued that the increasing share of AI borrowers could pull investment-grade spreads higher without a corresponding deterioration in every constituent's credit quality. For that longer comparison, his interpretation contrasts with an inflation-expectations explanation and leaves the supply of financing central even after a soft employment release.

Dallas Fed President Lorie Logan supplied a distinct policy qualification in Thursday remarks that became available within the current reporting window. Logan, an FOMC voter this year, estimated that the target range still needed to rise another 50 basis points or more to balance the Fed's employment and inflation risks. She distinguished a yield rise associated with stronger growth and a higher neutral rate from an increase in term premiums. Higher term premiums could slow activity and reduce the need for the Fed itself to tighten, she said, while continuing to seek a modestly restrictive policy stance.

That position was firmer than the patient timetable already articulated by Vice Chair Philip Jefferson, New York Fed President John Williams and Vice Chair for Supervision Michelle Bowman. Friday's payrolls gave their case fresh economic support rather than another new leadership signal. Former Bridgewater strategist Rebecca Patterson warned that October could bring dissents after September's unanimous increase. She judged that even 29,000 additional jobs represented positive growth when the breakeven employment pace was near zero, leaving room for disagreement over whether inflation or slowing recruitment should dominate the next decision.

Factory orders added a quieter, mixed demand observation. August orders rose 0.1%, matching consensus, after July growth was revised to 0.8% from 0.9%. Orders excluding transportation rose 0.3%, and those excluding defense increased 0.1%. Machinery orders gained 1.1% after 1.5%, electrical equipment, appliances and components rose 1% after no growth, and primary metals increased 1.2% after 2.1%. Nondefense aircraft and parts orders fell 4.3%, while fabricated metals declined 1.4%. The detail showed continuing demand in several investment categories alongside weakness elsewhere, rather than a second broad contraction signal following payrolls.

Risk assets held more of their initial relief. The S&P 500 closed up 0.73% at 7,722.72, the Nasdaq 100 gained 1% to 30,807.93, and semiconductor shares rose 2.40%. The VIX fell to 15.31. The Dollar Index declined 0.17% to 101.93; Bloomberg's separate dollar gauge fell 0.3%, its worst day in a month, but still gained about 0.8% over the week. Gold also failed to sustain its first response: spot bullion was down 0.92% at $4,139.13 an ounce at 1:35 p.m. New York time after earlier rising as much as 1.2%. The bond reversal continued to bear on assets sensitive to the return available on interest-paying securities.

## France's Wider Spreads Complicate the ECB's Inflation Fight

France's 10-year spread over Germany reached 154 basis points Friday, beyond the 141-basis-point level reported late Thursday. The further deterioration took the premium to its widest since 2011. The budget presentation had not arrested selling, and new reporting identified more clearly how concentrated leveraged positions were turning fiscal concern into abrupt market moves.

Taula Capital Management, Balyasny Asset Management and other firms had built carry positions exploiting the difference between French bond yields and interest-rate swaps, according to people familiar with their trades. They rushed to unwind when bonds fell Thursday. RBC BlueBay's Kaspar Hense reported stop-loss triggers both in steepener positions and in long-France trades. Fidelity's Marion Le Morhedec estimated that hedge funds accounted for probably half the current spread activity, adding pressure in a market whose investor base had become more dependent on fast-moving capital.

Longer-term investors were also changing allocations. Sumitomo Mitsui DS Asset Management's Shinji Kunibe said his global fixed-income funds had sold all their French government bonds, directing most proceeds into German bunds and some into short Japanese government debt. He contrasted France's fiscal uncertainty with Japan's increasing communication about the costs of its investment initiative. Credit Agricole Assurances' Florence Barjou still regarded France as a core holding but said the insurer was diversifying; it held approximately €61 billion of French sovereign debt in the first half of the year. These were different degrees of withdrawal, not a uniform abandonment by institutional holders.

Italy's 10-year spread over Germany stood at 127 basis points Friday and was heading for its largest weekly widening since March 2020. Spain's gap also grew. Weekend reporting of the week's trading added Belgium and Greece to the affected markets, while noting that the rout largely stabilized Friday and longer maturities recovered. Morgan Stanley Investment Management's Jeff Mueller described the first signs of contagion, with continued erratic price action a potential reason for policymakers to pay closer attention. The relative levels remained well below earlier crisis extremes in much of the region, but the speed of repricing made cross-market transmission the immediate concern.

The Swiss franc showed that investors were seeking protection outside euro-area debt as well as within it. It gained about 1.8% against the euro over two days, taking the pair to around 0.93 on Friday, a two-month low. CME trading volumes Thursday reached roughly four times their average this year. Commerzbank's Michael Pfister now expected the euro-franc pair at 0.91 in a year, citing Switzerland's more balanced budget. The move revived demand for a currency that had previously lost appeal because of its low interest-rate return.

The ECB's inflation problem became more pronounced on the same day. September euro-area consumer prices increased 3.8% from a year earlier, above the 3.7% consensus and August's 3.2%, reaching a three-year high. Core inflation rose to 2.5% as expected, and the services measure reached 3.2%. The regional release consolidated the previously reported national overshoots, with energy remaining the principal source of acceleration. European Commission surveys also showed selling-price expectations above long-run averages across sectors and a noticeable rise in households' expected inflation over the next year.

Bloomberg Economics' David Powell nevertheless saw less urgency than the headline suggested. Quarterly averages for headline and core inflation remained broadly consistent with ECB forecasts, he said; a base effect in airfares contributed to the underlying increase, while services inflation momentum weakened. Together with the sovereign-yield surge, that supported his expectation of no October increase and probably one final move in December. Following U.S. payrolls, money markets placed greater weight on two further ECB increases than three and on three Bank of England increases rather than four, after pricing more than 100 basis points for both as recently as Tuesday.

The policy challenge extends beyond the next rate decision. The ECB's unused Transmission Protection Instrument is intended to counter unwarranted, disorderly market dynamics that impair monetary-policy transmission. Danske Bank's Piet Christiansen argued that France's fiscal stance and political uncertainty warranted a wider spread, complicating a case for intervention. Purchasing bonds to relieve those pressures could look like deficit financing and ease conditions while the central bank was still trying to contain inflation.

Citigroup's Jamie Searle suggested pausing quantitative tightening as a possible earlier response. Resuming reinvestment would reduce the amount of debt price-sensitive buyers must absorb. Allianz Trade's Ana Boata put the French contribution from maturing ECB holdings at about €5 billion a month, roughly 20% of new issuance. That supplies a concrete reason why a balance-sheet adjustment could matter without an outright commitment to suppress a particular French yield premium.

There was no announcement of either intervention. Bundesbank President Joachim Nagel emphasized the 2% inflation mandate rather than a specific spread level, and Bank of France Governor Emmanuel Moulin warned that the ECB had no miracle solution. Global Sovereign Advisory's Anne-Laure Kiechel viewed a French-German spread near 175-180 basis points as a possible point for action, but that was her assessment, not an ECB threshold. Candriam CIO Nicolas Forest highlighted a separate obstacle to Outright Monetary Transactions: formal assistance would have to be requested, a politically difficult step under a potential Le Pen or Mélenchon government.

Fiscal choices elsewhere were moving in the opposite direction to calls for greater budget latitude. Italy made a late reduction in planned defense spending to bring its deficit below the EU's 3% ceiling. EU officials warned that governments seeking exemptions for energy support were underestimating the need for predictability in markets. Finland's Olli Rehn said higher borrowing costs and limited fiscal room could expose vulnerabilities elsewhere in the financial system, placing responsibility for sustained consolidation on governments. The new market stress therefore did not create agreement that fiscal limits should be relaxed.

## AI Financing Expands as New-Issue Demand Becomes Less Reliable

Broadcom's syndicate began gathering $60 billion of fresh AI chip financing intended to benefit Anthropic and other companies. Banks in the package led by Blackstone were preparing syndication letters for a $42 billion Class A senior-secured tranche, according to people familiar with the plans. The scale makes investor reception consequential well beyond the individual financing: it arrives as bond buyers are already digesting enormous acquisition and infrastructure borrowing.

Amazon was exploring a different route. The Financial Times reported discussions to move about $8 billion of high-end Nvidia chips off its balance sheet into a special-purpose vehicle financed by outside investors. The proposed assets comprise thousands of Grace Blackwell chips across more than a dozen U.S. data centers. Australian operator Firmus Grid, backed by Nvidia, priced its planned IPO at A$11 a share, seeking at least A$5 billion and implying a valuation around A$30 billion. Debt syndication, outside asset financing and public equity were offering different ways to fund the same capital-intensive expansion.

SoftBank illustrated how equity enthusiasm and creditor caution could diverge. Its shares gained 24% over four weeks and recorded their first positive month in four in September, while credit-default swaps reached their highest since 2023. A roughly 20% September recovery in Arm shares supported SoftBank's asset value, given its nearly 90% ownership of the chip designer. Yet SoftBank traded at a 24% discount to net asset value on September 29, wider than its 20% year-to-date average. Sparx Asset Management's Han Jiho argued that continued CDS widening could limit the share-price benefit from further gains in underlying assets.

The fresh equity recovery did not erase expensive debt funding. SoftBank's recent $11.1 billion junk sale included a 7.5-year bond yielding 9.75%. Bernstein's David Dai emphasized the potential upside from Arm's exposure to agentic AI and server CPUs, estimating that the CPU market could grow as large as $330 billion. Resona's Hiroki Takei saw higher borrowing costs as a tail risk while current earnings supplied financing capacity, but warned that leverage could make an eventual AI reversal severe. Their optimism relied on asset growth and cash generation rather than lower creditor demands.

The broader primary-market outlook was becoming more restrained. Weekend reporting found that Campbell's and Bain Capital Credit's private-credit fund had encountered lackluster bond demand, while Uzbekistan's Multinational Mine Group shelved a five-year note sale. Only four borrowers entered the U.S. high-grade market during the week. Expected October investment-grade issuance was around $100 billion, compared with $132 billion in October 2025 and nearly $195 billion in September, although year-to-date sales were still up about 30%.

Paramount's weak trading debut had already exposed that difficulty; Friday's additional disclosures quantified the issuer's own pricing benefit and remaining interest burden. CFO Dennis Cinelli said the company reduced borrowing costs by 37.5 basis points during marketing, saving about $200 million annually. Some investors withdrew as pricing tightened, leaving others with larger allocations than they expected. The transaction could be completed without making its securities easy to distribute afterward. Cinelli and Citi's Leon Kalvaria remained positive about the financing's long-term purpose and execution, while buyers had borne immediate markdowns.

A separate weekend account identified a more specific link between Paramount and Oracle. Investors increasingly treated their default risk as connected through Larry Ellison, with the cost of insuring the two companies' debt converging and moving together. The family trust guaranteed a significant portion of approximately $47 billion of acquisition equity financing, and the family had pledged steps to help Paramount reduce leverage. Much of Ellison's wealth, however, remained tied to Oracle shares as Oracle undertook its own debt-funded AI buildout.

Ellison's fortune had declined by almost $200 billion from its peak but still stood around $192 billion, according to Bloomberg's billionaire estimates. Oracle's long-term debt exceeded $160 billion after nearly doubling over two years, making it the fifth-largest borrower in the U.S. corporate-bond market. S&P had reduced Oracle to BBB- in July and Paramount's issuer rating to BB in September. Wellington's Campe Goodman said the common sponsor created a combined exposure, while S&P's Jawad Hussain highlighted the risk that an Oracle share decline could weaken family support precisely when Paramount needed capital. The connection concerns the financial capacity behind a pledge, not identical operating businesses.

Across global corporate debt, spreads widened about 5 basis points over the week to their widest in half a year. A global comparison of market yields with existing coupons reached 1.23 percentage points, up from 0.17 in February, illustrating the greater cost of replacing old borrowings. Those weekly conditions coexisted with Friday's modest tightening in broad U.S. credit spreads. LQD's distribution-adjusted daily return was minus 0.20%, while HYG gained about 0.01% and EMB lost 0.13%, as the renewed rise in Treasury yields continued to affect total returns.

Barclays strategists Harry Mateer and Dominique Toublan reported Friday that a 10-year Treasury rise of at least 40 basis points over a month had typically preceded later corporate-spread widening. PGIM's David Del Vecchio judged rate volatility a more immediate demand constraint than spreads themselves. Higher all-in yields could eventually attract pension and other income buyers, he said, but investors wanted greater rate stability before committing capital more aggressively. The tightening on Friday did not resolve the uncertainty over where the underlying financing rate would settle.

## Property, Private Credit and Sovereign Disclosure Draw Scrutiny

Property-focused banks were a pronounced weak spot in European subordinated debt. Deutsche Pfandbriefbank's AT1 securities fell below 80 cents on the euro and were Europe's worst AT1 performers in September. Its €300 million issue, which passed its first call date three years earlier, lost more than 9% since August. Landesbank Baden-Württemberg's €750 million issue, callable in 2030, was indicated below par Friday for the first time in more than a year.

The euro-hedged AT1 index had moved from gains into a 2% total-return loss since August. PBB describes commercial real estate financing as the core of its business, while property represents almost a fifth of LBBW's exposures. Higher rates weaken property values and borrower metrics, increasing stress on existing loans while reducing new lending opportunities. TwentyFour's Jakub Lichwa said some German banks' commercial real estate portfolios had already weakened before the latest rates selloff, creating overlapping pressures. Outside banking, German apartment buyer Net Zero Properties abandoned a €500 million borrowing plan after improved terms failed to secure sufficient demand.

Bain Capital was exploring an investment in Hong Kong's New World Development, potentially alongside fresh capital from the controlling Cheng family, according to people familiar with the discussions. New World's debt stood around HK$143 billion at June's end, with a portion due in 2028. Its shares briefly rose on news of the talks before again trading down 2.3% at 3:43 p.m. Hong Kong time Friday. Negotiations remained open, with no certainty of a transaction. The prospect concerned new support for a debt-heavy developer rather than an agreed recapitalization.

Private-credit investors were encountering continuing limits on liquidity. Blue Owl again capped quarterly redemptions at 5% in two funds. Shareholders in the approximately $5 billion technology-focused OTIC sought to withdraw 39% of shares in Q3, slightly above the previous 38.1%. After its latest payment, the fund would have supplied about $446 million of liquidity over six months, equivalent to 35% of original tender requests. Requests at the $35 billion Blue Owl Credit Income Corp. eased to 16.8% from 18.8%, but remained well above the amount redeemed.

Valuation practices were receiving closer official attention as those requests persisted. An SEC staff statement pressed firms to improve how private holdings were valued and how risks and values were disclosed, without introducing new rules. Apollo began rolling out daily prices across its $850 billion credit business Thursday. Ares separately raised $4.2 billion for its first secondaries fund, more than four times its initial target, to supply capital to private managers. The developments addressed valuation frequency and liquidity provision through different channels; neither changed the redemption terms at Blue Owl.

Gabon supplied a sovereign disclosure problem with an immediate funding consequence. Investor calls for a proposed $580 million bond drew questions about consolidated debt of CFA9.53 trillion, or approximately $16.3 billion, and a projected 2027 deficit of 5.4% of GDP. The debt figure was 19% below a CFA11.7 trillion estimate published September 13, yet above July's CFA9.4 trillion end-2025 figure. July's accompanying statement had led some investors to expect a significant decline after an audit, making the later presentation difficult to reconcile with that expectation.

The 2033 dollar bond's yield rose as much as 150 basis points over the week to a record 13.1%, before retreating Friday to around 12.98%. Gabon's dollar debt was the weakest among frontier sovereigns for the week through October 2. Participants in the calls said the rise could hamper the planned sale; the government did not say whether it would postpone issuance. The new issue was not simply global yields rising but investors questioning how the reported liabilities had changed.

Indonesia's new finance minister offered a contrasting attempt to clarify institutional boundaries. Suahasil Nazara said Friday that he would keep the deficit within its legal 3%-of-GDP ceiling and leave monetary policy and the Danantara wealth fund to their own mandates. Danantara dividends were not included in either the 2026 or 2027 budget, departing from his predecessor's effort to seek nearly $7 billion for the state. He also ruled out reviving daily government bond buybacks, judging current conditions insufficient to activate the stabilization framework, and described the Indonesia-U.S. 10-year gap of about 220-225 basis points as healthy.

Suahasil said another global bond sale was possible this quarter after May's $3.45 billion dollar-and-euro transaction. The April 2036 dollar bond traded around 106 basis points over Treasuries, its widest in about two months. The budget forecasts remained demanding: a 2.85% deficit this year was expected to narrow to 2.4% in 2027, assuming oil at $75 a barrel and an average rupiah of 17,500 per dollar. Oil was above $100 and the currency near 18,000. He defended coordination with Danantara without directly resolving concerns about fiscal risks outside the headline deficit that Fitch and Moody's had highlighted when changing their outlooks to negative.

Municipal credit had its own funding decision. Moody's cut Manhattan's Nightingale-Bamford School to Baa1 from A3 and changed the outlook to stable from negative as the school planned to use about $10 million of unrestricted reserves for an athletics project while fundraising continued. Debt outstanding was almost $64 million in fiscal 2025, and the project cost was set at $90 million. Moody's cited execution and governance risks around the capital campaign and changes in fundraising leadership, while preserving its favorable assessment of demand, pricing power, operating improvement and liquidity. Construction remained on schedule and within budget.

## Inflation Divergence and New Institutional Developments

Tokyo's September core consumer inflation accelerated to 2.7% from 1.8%, above the 2.3% median forecast and back above 2% for the first time since January. Inflation excluding both fresh food and energy rose to 3% from 2%. The expiry of childcare and water-charge relief contributed substantially, but government energy subsidies were still reducing the overall gauge by almost 0.4 percentage point.

The detail extended beyond the reversal of temporary discounts. Processed-food prices rose 3.6%; major food and beverage companies increased prices on 4,965 items during September, more than twice the year-earlier number, according to Teikoku Databank. Water-service costs increased about 66%, lodging moved to a 4.6% annual increase from a 1.4% decline, and service prices rose 2.3%, their strongest gain since November 2023. Daiichi Life's Yoshiki Shinke expected a December BOJ increase, arguing that higher costs were reaching consumers even after allowing for the temporary measures.

Economic Policy Minister Minoru Kiuchi qualified an earlier suggestion that Japan no longer needed monetary easing. He said Friday that he had meant extraordinary tools such as yield-curve control, which ended in March 2024, and declined to say whether conventional easing remained necessary. He also declined to elaborate on the Cabinet Office representative's neutral-rate remarks at the September meeting. The clarification left government acceptance of further ordinary rate increases less explicit than some investors had inferred from earlier ministerial comments.

Australia's relative bond performance was moving in a different direction. Its 10-year yield stood only about 12 basis points above the U.S. equivalent, near the narrowest gap since September 2025. Barrenjoey and Westpac expected convergence in coming months, while NAB's Kenneth Crompton said inversion could occur before his 2027 base case and that the gap might revisit minus 20 basis points by the end of next year if policy expectations diverged sufficiently. Australian government bonds lost 1% in September against a 2.2% decline in Treasuries. The country's fiscal position and smaller AI-related financing demand supplied distinctions beyond the already reported RBA policy decision; sensitivity to U.S. rates and renewed domestic inflation remained constraints on further relative gains.

Fresh research quantified Britain's additional financing penalty. Bloomberg Economics estimated a credibility premium of around 30 basis points on benchmark debt, implying £2.5 billion of added annual interest costs by 2029-2030. Schroders' James Bilson saw the difficulty partly as a reputation problem, while RBC's Cathal Kennedy pointed to skepticism about fiscal plans that had repeatedly failed to be delivered. The estimate concerned an extra country-specific cost within the global yield rise, not a new 6% long-gilt milestone.

There was also a prospective change in local British borrowing. The government encouraged English mayors to consider borrowing against revenue from a proposed overnight visitor levy, with legislation still to be tabled and local plans expected by early 2028. UKHospitality's Allen Simpson objected that opposition parties had pledged to scrap the tax, potentially removing revenue underpinning long-lived debt. The financing proposal would bring infrastructure spending forward, but the political durability of its pledged income remained disputed.

In the U.S., Scope kept its AA- sovereign rating and stable outlook in a Friday statement, while warning that large deficits left the country increasingly exposed to changes in investor sentiment. It projected debt at 160% of output within a decade and exceptionally high net interest costs by 2031 unless growth strengthened materially or fiscal adjustment followed. The unchanged rating came with a more explicit warning about the medium-term trajectory, not another downgrade.

Federal Reserve governance also received a new decision. Attorney General Todd Blanche said Friday that the Justice Department would not reopen its criminal investigation of former chair Jerome Powell on the basis of the inspector general's renovation findings. An independent audit could still prompt investigation if it uncovered criminal wrongdoing. On Sunday, National Economic Council Director Kevin Hassett called for Powell to leave the board and disagreed with September's rate increase, while saying he respected Chair Kevin Warsh's reasons for it. The weekend intervention renewed political pressure after Blanche's decision; it was a later development, separate from Friday's bond trading.

ECB succession discussions advanced as well. German Chancellor Friedrich Merz planned meetings with Klaas Knot in the coming days and Pablo Hernández de Cos in the next few weeks, according to people familiar with the deliberations. The contacts indicated that Berlin was no longer considering Joachim Nagel for the presidency. Italy's Giancarlo Giorgetti asked Lagarde Friday for greater clarity about her future. The developments added concrete meetings and a public request for guidance to the existing succession process, with no decision on the presidency.

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent offered a weekend response to the yield selloff in an Axios interview published Saturday. He said a global rather than uniquely U.S. increase did not warrant alarm, emphasized strong consumption and wage growth, and expected the Iran-related energy shock eventually to fade. His confidence contrasted with concerns about how persistent financing costs would affect weaker parts of the economy. Franklin Templeton's Max Gokhman estimated that only about 13% of U.S. nonfinancial corporate debt, roughly $570 billion, matured in 2027, while many existing homeowners retained mortgages averaging around 4%. Those buffers delay the effect of high new borrowing rates; they make its duration consequential rather than removing the exposure.

## Forward Market Significance

The next U.S. growth test arrives October 5 with final S&P Global services and composite PMIs at 9:45 a.m. New York time. Consensus calls for services at 58.7 after 56.5 and the composite at 58.4 after 56. ISM services follows at 10 a.m., with a 55.7 consensus against 55.4 previously. Strong services demand would sit differently beside weak payroll recruitment than a broader slowdown, while price and hiring detail will bear on the remaining case for another Fed increase. Weekly ADP employment on October 6 and claims on October 8 will add more timely labor observations; initial claims are expected at 195,000 after 197,000.

The Fed's September minutes are due Wednesday, followed by the ECB's meeting account Thursday. Both describe decisions taken before Friday's employment report and the latest French spread stress, so the important question is how durable their inflation concerns remain under the changed conditions. Williams, Bowman and Logan are scheduled to speak October 6, offering separate perspectives on patience, further restraint and the contribution from higher market yields. U.S. CPI on October 14 remains a consequential inflation test before the October 27-28 Fed meeting.

Treasury auctions of three-, 10- and 30-year debt during the coming week will test demand after the failed payroll rally. The three-year sale is scheduled October 6; the longer maturities confront the competition for capital most directly. Corporate dealers expect $25 billion-$30 billion of U.S. high-grade sales during the week, while more than 80% of surveyed European professionals anticipate over €25 billion. Reception to new deals will show whether attractive absolute yields begin to offset rate instability. Broadcom's planned syndication is a distinct test of financing appetite for AI, and Paramount's expected October 6 acquisition closing shifts attention toward execution after the placement of its debt.

Euro-area finance ministers meet in Luxembourg Thursday with energy support, fiscal flexibility and France's bond turmoil pressing on the agenda. Further spillover into other sovereigns would sharpen the question of monetary transmission and the ECB's balance-sheet response. Japan's August wages Tuesday will test whether real-pay growth extended to an eighth month, while India's Wednesday policy decision is expected to raise the repo rate to 5.5%. Britain's October 28 budget must address the credibility penalty attached to its fiscal plans as well as the global rise in rates.

Energy has moved from emergency-stock discussion to an announced release. The G7 and partners agreed Friday to supply as much as 100 million barrels of oil and diesel over four months, coordinated by the IEA and initially emphasizing diesel. The agreement reduced the likelihood of a U.S. diesel-export ban and pushed European diesel and Brent prices lower on the news. At Friday's fixed-income close, WTI was down 1.90% at $91.11, while Brent was only 0.06% lower at $102.25 and still up 4.94% for the week. The pace at which refined fuel reaches consumers remains material to inflation and fiscal-support needs.

In the separate early Asian session Monday, Brent for December delivery rose above $103 as Yemen began a bid to recapture Houthi-controlled areas, while major OPEC+ producers had agreed to leave next month's output quotas unchanged. Nasdaq 100 futures gained about 0.2%, extending the equity response to Friday's jobs report rather than establishing a new Treasury outcome. Brazil's presidential vote had taken place Sunday and counting was still under way. The unresolved result, alongside renewed energy pressure, leaves independent risks for the next session after the completed U.S. close.

overall_summary.headline: Treasuries lose their payroll rally as weaker hiring fails to lower long-term borrowing costs
overall_summary.session_narrative:
Treasuries reversed their initial rally after September payrolls rose only 29,000 against a 90,000 consensus and annual wage growth slowed to 3%, its weakest since 2021. Swaps reduced the chance of an October Fed increase to about 20% from nearly 30% before the release, yet traders again anticipated a year-end move by the session's end. The benchmark 10-year yield was around 5.27% late Friday; Bloomberg's dated 10-year yield rose 5.7 basis points to 5.273%, with its real counterpart up 2.7 basis points and same-series breakeven inflation up 3 basis points. Relief over the next meeting did not secure lower long-term financing costs.

France's 10-year premium over Germany reached 154 basis points, its widest since 2011, as leveraged-position exits intensified selling. Euro-area inflation accelerated to 3.8%, leaving the ECB to weigh further restraint against sovereign financing stress. AI funding needs added a separate pressure: Broadcom's syndicate began gathering $60 billion of financing as corporate buyers sought more rate stability before committing capital.

U.S. investment-grade and high-yield spreads tightened modestly, while hard-currency emerging-market spreads tightened noticeably. Equities retained their gains as bonds lost theirs. The G7's agreed emergency oil and diesel release eased fuel-price anxiety, although Brent remained above $102 a barrel at the fixed-income close. Upcoming growth and inflation releases, alongside Treasury auctions and new corporate deals, will test whether policy patience can coexist with sustained demand for financing.
